about: Which page of the SDK reference (docs/sdkref.json, format mfx-sdkref/1) each public type of com.mfxhub.sdk is on, in display order, with the page's Java intro. Page ids and their order are the shared page list's; a page's title and summary are not here, because the docs site takes them from that list. A nested type follows the type it is in. Every public type is on exactly one page: the generator refuses one that is on none.

pages.intro: `MfxClient` signs every request with your Ed25519 key, retries reads within a budget and opens the stream. Build one with `MfxClient.builder(baseUrl, keyId, signingKey)` and close it with try-with-resources. Every call is asynchronous and returns a `CompletableFuture`; a list is also an `Iterable` that follows the cursor.

`client.terminals()` provisions, reads, restarts, drains and retires the terminals your key's tenant owns; `client.farms()`, `client.maintenance()` and `client.expertAdvisors()` say where they run, when they pause and which expert advisors they carry.

`client.execution()` places and changes orders. Every method completes with an `ExecutionResult` and never exceptionally: a timeout, a refusal and a broker rejection are all results with a reason. Decimals are `BigDecimal`, and the idempotency key is always yours.
`client.tradingAccounts()` reads and trades the accounts your tenant holds on every venue, with the same commands as `execution()`.

`client.accounts()` reads what a terminal sees of its account; `client.catalog()` says which brokers, servers and symbols you can point a terminal at; `client.usage()` says how much of each limit is used.
`client.md()` subscribes to ticks, depth and candles, delivered on the stream, and reads history.

`client.stream()` opens one WebSocket for many channels, resumable by sequence number across reconnects. `MfxStream` is an `Iterable` of `StreamEvent`; `Events.eventOf` reads a message as its typed event, and `LiveAccount` keeps an account's view current from it.
`client.risk()` manages risk policies, challenge plans and the accounts they cover, and reads what the rules did.
`client.copy()` runs copy trading: leaders, followers and their mandates, groups, signals, and what each copy did.
`client.billing()` reads the billing standing and the invoices, and says what clears a payment that is due.
`client.tenant()` reads what your organisation must accept; `client.webhooks()` manages webhook endpoints and verifies each delivery.

A read or a write that the platform refuses completes exceptionally with an `MfxApiException` of the kind its code names; a fault on the way is an `MfxTransportException`. Execution methods never complete exceptionally: they complete with a result. Every exception is unchecked.
